followup_explanation:
This was an open-ended creative generation task (writing a shop bio), and a few factors pointed to Willet-235B:

1. **Higher benchmarks across the board** — Willet leads on Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 83.2), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.3), and every internal eval category, including Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7, though that gap is within tie territory).

2. **Task preference fit** — Lapwing self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work; its preference declines as task latitude increases, and this bio request is exactly that kind of loosely-specified creative task. Willet has no such aversion. Note that this is about self-reported preference, not capability — both models are documented as equally capable regardless of preference — but with everything else roughly equal, I'd rather route an open-ended creative task to the model that isn't documented as averse to it.

The user's frustration ("don't churn out the usual generic nonsense") signals they want a genuinely engaged, non-formulaic response, which made the preference-fit consideration more relevant than usual.
